outcome.technical: tools/_suite.py: shared marker helpers (MARKER_NAME, git_dir_of, pid_alive, hold, release, marker_state: none/live/stale/unreadable). tools/prove-gates.py main(): holds the marker under the git dir for the whole mutating run (refuses to start if another live/unreadable one exists, releases in finally; --list/--help take none). tools/sweep-selftests.py: marker_gate() refuses with exit 2 naming the marker file and pid on a live or unreadable marker, ignores a dead pid's and prints 'ignoring stale marker'. tools/orchestrator-state.py: sweep_line() prints 'MUTATING SWEEP: a mutating sweep is live (pid, since)'. CONTRIBUTING.md note added; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md untouched (it does not describe tools/). New cases mk0-mk2 (sweep) and o1-o3 (orchestrator-state). Exit codes: sweep 0 (331 files ok), --spaced 0, ruff 0 (after fixing one F821 I introduced), vermin 0, gate-parity 0, prove-gates --selftest 0. Not run: a full mutating prove-gates run, so the live marker is exercised only through the helper cases, not end to end. orchestrator-state now imports _suite (and so the test tree) on each run.
outcome.descriptive: A mutating gate sweep announces itself via a git-dir marker; the sweep refuses to read a tree mid-mutation and orchestrator-state reports it.

claims: claims: marker is per-worktree git dir (a sweep in another worktree reads a different tree); stale = pid not alive per os.kill(0) / OpenProcess; pid reuse by an unrelated process would read as live (accepted).
